problem: Show that for any Poisson-binomial law with variance V >= 1, the normalized Turan deficit delta_D = 1 - f_{D-1} f_{D+1} / f_D^2 at the first descent index D satisfies V*delta_D >= 1/4, so the variance alone forces a lower bound on strict log-concavity near the mode.
debate: The quantitative log-concavity and mode literature on Bernoulli sums (Hillion-Johnson ultra-log-concavity bound, Johnson, Darroch, Pitman, Dumbgen-Wellner, Bobkov-Marsiglietti-Melbourne), which the opening cites as a set of results and not as a named debate.
gap: Known lower bounds on delta_k depend on the number of summands n or on the success probabilities and degenerate when summands with p_i near 0 and near 1 accumulate at fixed variance, while the mode and mass-ratio results do not control delta_k at all.
contribution: A variance-only bound V*delta_D >= 1/4 (with a binomial family showing no constant above 1/3 works), extended by Hillion-Johnson cubics to delta_k >= 1/(4V+|k-D|), with the key one-variable inequality proved by computer-assisted Bernstein expansions in exact arithmetic.
note: The result is stated cleanly, but you never say who needs a Turan deficit at the first descent beyond a normal-curvature analogy and one unitary-matrix example, so open with the consumer of the bound, and say why the 1/4 versus 1/3 gap is acceptable.
